jezero.name: Jezero Crater
jezero.blurb: Ancient lake with a river delta: clays and carbonates that may preserve signs of past life.

targets.name: Delta-front cliff-base outcrop
targets.why: The ~26° cliff cuts through delta sediments and exposes ancient lake layers. Its base is covered by dark ripples, so reaching it means crossing soft sand.

targets.name: Crater-rim ejecta
targets.why: A ~350 m impact crater brought deep rock to the surface, so several layers can be sampled in one stop.

targets.name: Delta-top sediments
targets.why: The delta top is ~100 m above the plains; the planner decides whether it can be climbed safely.

targets.name: Dark ripple field below the cliff
targets.why: Low night-time temperature in THEMIS (low thermal inertia) plus dark, smooth texture: loose sand where a rover can bog down.

jezero.goal: Sample delta lake sediments that could preserve signs of ancient life.

gale.name: Gale Crater
gale.blurb: Foot of Mount Sharp: layered mudstones of an old lake and the active Bagnold dune field.

targets.name: Bagnold dune field edge
targets.why: An active basaltic dune: darkest in HiRISE and coldest at night in THEMIS (loose sand). CRISM shows olivine, as Curiosity measured at Namib Dune.

targets.name: Murray formation bedrock
targets.why: Pale lake mudstone ~170 m up the lower slopes of Mount Sharp; the climb dominates the energy budget.

targets.name: Fractured butte margin
targets.why: The roughest ground on the map: boulders and fractures. A good test of whether the planner refuses a route.

targets.name: Marias Pass (Curiosity, sols ~990–1060)
targets.why: Curiosity drove through here in 2015 and drilled the 'Buckskin' sample nearby. Real rover photos are pinned around it.

gale.goal: Measure active dune sand and old lake mudstone at the foot of Mount Sharp.

jezero_delta.name: Jezero Delta Front
jezero_delta.blurb: The front of the ancient river delta, where Perseverance studied and sampled layered rock in 2022.
jezero_delta.goal: Trace the carbonate and clay layers of the delta that Perseverance sampled in 2022.

targets.name: Carbonate-bearing layers
targets.why: CRISM sees a carbonate signature here. On Earth, carbonates that form in lakes can trap organic matter.

targets.name: Clay-rich fan sediments
targets.why: Fe/Mg clay in CRISM and warm at night in THEMIS: consolidated fine sediment laid down in water.

targets.name: Upper fan viewpoint
targets.why: The highest point of the site, ~140 m above the habitat: a view over the whole delta front.

targets.name: Perseverance stop, sol 715
targets.why: Where Perseverance parked on sol 715; real rover photos are pinned here.

gale_boxwork.name: Gale Boxwork
gale_boxwork.blurb: High on Mount Sharp: a web of boxwork ridges that Curiosity explored in 2025.
gale_boxwork.goal: Study the boxwork ridges: mineral veins left by groundwater as Gale dried out.

targets.name: Boxwork ridges (Curiosity, 2025)
targets.why: Low ridges of cemented rock in a honeycomb pattern, thought to be minerals left by groundwater. Curiosity drove here around sol 4625.

targets.name: Clay-bearing bench
targets.why: Fe/Mg clay signature in CRISM next to the boxwork: compare the rock between the ridges.

targets.name: Upper Mount Sharp overlook
targets.why: ~600 m above the habitat. A test of whether the planner says no: most approaches are over 25°.

targets.name: Dark sand trough
targets.why: Darkest ground and coldest at night: loose sand in a trough between ridges.

mawrth.name: Mawrth Vallis
mawrth.mission: No rover yet · former landing-site finalist
mawrth.blurb: One of the most clay-rich places on Mars. Never visited: a scouting site for a future crew.
mawrth.goal: Scout one of the most clay-rich terrains on Mars as a future human landing site.

targets.name: Light-toned layered rock
targets.why: The bright layers of Mawrth Vallis are among the most clay-rich rocks seen from orbit; CRISM coverage here is partial.

targets.name: Possible carbonate signal
targets.why: One of the few CRISM-covered spots in this site shows a carbonate-like index. Worth a closer look.

targets.name: Olivine-bearing dark cap
targets.why: Darker capping rock with an olivine signature, younger than the clay layers below.

targets.name: Dark mantling sand
targets.why: Darkest and coldest at night: loose material that a rover should avoid.
